samples.summary: `Selection.getSelectedText()` still resolves a cell rectangle with the flat `layout.blocks.find()` this change replaced everywhere else — a nested-table rectangle yields empty `text/plain` on copy AND on cut
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:761-763: `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId); if (!lb?.block.tableData) return '';`. A nested table block is not a member of `layout.blocks` (that is the whole premise of the diff's fixes to `normalizeRange` at selection.ts:128 and `getSelectedTableCells` at text-editor.ts:4331), so this returns `''`. Both clipboard writers call it unconditionally right after the now-fixed rich flavour: text-editor.ts:1439 (copy) and text-editor.ts:1482 (cut). Cut then calls `this.deleteSelection()` at text-editor.ts:1484, so a user cutting a cell rectangle inside a nested table — a gesture this change newly makes reachable by shift+click — loses the content for any external paste target that only reads `text/plain`. Fix belongs here: use `resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` as the fallback, exactly as the two sibling sites now do.

samples.summary: The cycle guard the diff adds to three parent-chain walks is bypassed by two unguarded walks in the very function it edited (`normalizeRange`), which hang on the same cyclic `blockParentMap`
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:147-157: `while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex((lb) => lb.block.id === anchorTopId) === -1) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(anchorTopId); if (!parentInfo) break; anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` (and the identical focus walk at :153). With the cyclic map the diff's own new test constructs (`a -> b -> a`, nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:253-258) neither id is ever found in `layout.blocks`, `parentInfo` is always defined, and the loop never terminates. This runs on every non-cell-range selection normalization — i.e. on virtually every render with a selection — so it is strictly more reachable than the `resolveNestedTableLayout` walk the diff hardened. Fix belongs on these two loops (add the same `seen` set).

samples.summary: `resolvePositionPixel()` walks the same peer-written parent chain with an unguarded `while (true)` and an unbounded `unshift`, so the hang the new guard prevents is still reachable through peer cursor painting
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:122-127: `while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(currentTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo); currentTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`. Identical shape to the walk hardened at table-layout.ts:489 and to `findOuterCellAddress`/`findOutermostTableId` in text-editor.ts; on a cyclic chain it spins forever and additionally grows `nestingPath` without bound (OOM as well as hang). This path runs per render for the local caret and for every peer cursor/selection, i.e. it is driven by remote presence data. Fix belongs on this loop.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim: selection.ts:761-763 resolves the cell-range table with the flat `layout.blocks.find()` and returns '' when it misses. The premise that a nested table is absent from `layout.blocks` is asserted by the repo's own fixed siblings (selection.ts:121-130, text-editor.ts:4326-4333), which both add the `resolveNestedTableLayout(...)?.dataBlock.tableData` fallback that getSelectedText lacks. The path is reachable: resolveCellGesture builds a tableCellRange whose blockId is the inner table id (text-editor.ts:3967-3982), and handleCopy/handleCut call getSelectedText unconditionally on the cell path (text-editor.ts:1439, 1482), with handleCut then deleting the selection (text-editor.ts:1484). No upstream guard blocks a nested-table cell range from reaching this branch, so the site is genuinely broken (empty text/plain on copy, and content loss for plain-text-only paste targets after cut). Major under the blast-radius rubric: an unupdated consumer of the resolution contract the change fixed elsewhere.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:146-157 contains two parent-chain walks over layout.blockParentMap whose only exits are "id present in layout.blocks" or "no parent entry"; with a cyclic chain (a -> b -> a) where neither id is in layout.blocks, parentInfo is always defined and the loop never terminates. No seen/visited set exists in selection.ts (grep for seen|visited|cycle across packages/docs/src returns hits only in table-layout.ts, range-slices.ts, text-editor.ts). The guard the finding references is real: packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:487-495 walks the same map with a `seen` set and returns undefined on a cycle, with a comment (table-layout.ts:480-486) stating block ids come verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes so a looping chain is representable and an unbounded walk would hang the tab; the same hardening appears at model/range-slices.ts:81-88 and view/text-editor.ts:3894-3906,3919-3924. The repo's own test (packages/docs/test/view/nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:251-261) builds exactly that cyclic map with blocks: []. The unguarded loops run on the ordinary non-cell-range selection path, reached from computeSelectionRects (selection.ts:562), Selection.getNormalizedRange (selection.ts:741), getSelectionRects (selection.ts:751) and getSelectedText (selection.ts:755), and execute before the hardened resolveNestedTableLayout call at selection.ts:169, so the guard does not cover them. This is the blast-radius lane: a cycle guard added to sibling walks with an unguarded path over the same data still reachable. Severity is a hang/tab freeze on a reachable render path, so it is blocking.

verdict.reason:
The finding is present exactly as described and is a genuine blast-radius bypass of the guard the change added.

1. The code is present verbatim: `packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:119-127` builds `nestingPath` with `nestingPath.push(cellInfo)` then an unguarded `while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(currentTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo); currentTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`. There is no visited set, no iteration cap, and no bound on `nestingPath`, so a `blockParentMap` chain that loops back on itself spins forever while growing the array (hang + unbounded memory).

2. The hardened counterpart confirms the invariant the change now assumes: `packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:487-495` performs the same walk but with `const seen = new Set<string>([topTableId])` and `if (seen.has(parentInfo.tableBlockId)) return undefined`. Its own comment at table-layout.ts:480-486 states that "Block ids arrive verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes (`crdt-tree.ts`), so a parent chain that loops back on itself — a duplicated or hostile id — is representable" and that an unbounded walk "would hang the tab". That is the threat model the change itself asserts; peer-cursor.ts is a second entry point into the identical walk that never passes through the new guard.

3. The unguarded walk is reachable on hot render paths, not dead code: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2039` calls `resolvePositionPixel(peer.position, ...)` inside `for (const peer of peerCursors)` during render — i.e. driven directly by remote presence data; `packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:73` calls it for the local caret's pixel position; and `packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:276-277` calls it for both selection endpoints. `resolvePositionPixel` is also a public export at `packages/docs/src/index.ts:189`. Entry into the loop only requires `layout.blockParentMap.get(position.blockId)` to be truthy (peer-cursor.ts:114-115), i.e. any caret inside a table cell.

No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable: the `seen` set in table-layout.ts is local to `resolveNestedTableLayout` and is never consulted by peer-cursor.ts, which reads `layout.blockParentMap` directly. This is squarely in the blast-radius lane ("a new guard with a way around it") and the impact at the bypassing site — an infinite loop plus unbounded allocation on a path fed by remote peer data — is major-or-worse, so it is blocking.

finding.summary: Sibling flat-lookup site `getSelectedTableCells()` was not updated, so the clipboard still cannot see a nested table's cell rectangle that selection.ts now paints
finding.evidence: The diff replaces the flat `layout.blocks.find(...)` in `normalizeRange()` with a `resolveNestedTableLayout()` fallback, but `TextEditor.getSelectedTableCells()` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4269) still does exactly the old thing: `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId); if (!lb?.block.tableData) return null;`. A nested table is not in `layout.blocks`, so a cell rectangle inside an inner table yields `null` cells for copy/cut, while the deletion path one screen away (text-editor.ts:4114) resolves the same id through `this.doc.getBlock(cr.blockId)`, which *does* walk into cells. Cut of a nested cell rectangle therefore clears cells (4116-4128) with nothing captured for the clipboard. The change makes this divergence visible/wider because the painted rectangle for the nested case is now merge-expanded while the copy path still bails out entirely. Fix belongs at 4269 (use `resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` as selection.ts now does).

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `getSelectedTableCells()` still performs the old flat `layout.blocks.find(...)` lookup and bails with `null` for a nested table. It does not. The method is at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4317 (not 4269 — that line is inside the unrelated multi-block delete `isFullSelection` computation), and at lines 4331-4334 it already applies precisely the fallback the finding prescribes: `layout.blocks.find(...)?.block.tableData ?? resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData`, mirroring selection.ts:128-130 exactly, with the resolver imported at text-editor.ts:21. The in-code comment at 4326-4330 records this very nested-table divergence (#1049) as handled here. The sibling `getSelectedBlocks()` also resolves via `resolveNestedTableLayout` (4379-4381). So the claimed asymmetry with the delete path (text-editor.ts:4169-4185, which resolves through `this.doc.getBlock`) does not exist, and the described cut-loses-clipboard-data scenario has no code to stand on.
